title: UN Calls for Sweeping Social Media Reforms and Changes at Meta
seoTitle: UN Demands Social Media Reforms and Changes at Meta
subtitle: The United Nations indicates the entire industry must undergo adjustments, while California's Attorney General assesses teen safety measures on TikTok and YouTube.
excerpt: The UN recommends broad social media reforms alongside changes at Meta, while California's Attorney General examines teen safety on TikTok and YouTube.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The United Nations (UN) has stated that any comprehensive reform of social media platforms must be accompanied by changes at Meta, the parent company of services such as Facebook and Instagram. The recommendation indicates that platform governance structures and content policies must evolve together to ensure consistency in digital protection and accountability measures.

What a Broad Social Media Reform Entails

A comprehensive reform typically involves revising terms of service, moderation mechanisms, algorithm transparency, and defining corporate accountability toward users and governments. In the UN's view, these changes should not occur in isolation; they must be aligned with adjustments to internal policies at Meta, which accounts for a substantial share of global social traffic.

California Attorney General Initiative

In parallel, the California Attorney General is scrutinizing two of the largest video platforms—TikTok and YouTube—with the aim of implementing teen-focused safety features. This review seeks to identify measures that can protect minors from inappropriate content, data collection practices, and other age-specific vulnerabilities.

The investigation focuses on developing tools that give young users better control over what they see, as well as features facilitating parental oversight. While specific solutions have yet to be detailed, the initiative highlights growing interest among state authorities to tailor platform policies to the safety needs of younger users.

Ongoing Context

In an environment where social media use has become an integral part of daily life, debates surrounding regulation and child protection are frequent. By recommending joint reforms, the UN emphasizes the importance of a coordinated approach among various stakeholders across the digital ecosystem. At the same time, local authorities, such as the California Attorney General, continue to pursue practical solutions addressing specific safety demands for vulnerable groups, including teenagers.

With information from BBC News.
